title: A transient Stripe `paymentIntents.retrieve` failure silently orphans the live escrow hold and re-points the ledger at a brand-new, unconfirmed PaymentIntent
summary: The reconcile-vs-recreate block is entirely gated on `existingPI` being non-null, and the retrieve that produces it swallows every error into a bare `catch (_)`. Any transient Stripe failure (429, 5xx, socket abort) makes the function skip the comparison AND the cancel, mint a second PaymentIntent, and overwrite `payments.payment_intent_id` with it — leaving the genuine `requires_capture` authorization live, unreferenced, and invisible to every control.
trigger: Booking B is `confirmed` (or `pending`) with a genuine hold PI_1 at `requires_capture`; `payments` = {PI_1, status:'authorized', amount_cents: authorizedCents}. The poster reopens the accept modal (web `AcceptPaymentModal`'s `useEffect` re-calls `createPaymentIntent` on every mount/booking-id change; mobile `GigsScreen.handleAccept` re-calls it on every Accept tap) — `canHold` permits both `pending` and `confirmed`, so the call proceeds. `stripe.paymentIntents.retrieve(PI_1)` throws once (Stripe 429/5xx/network). `existingPI` stays null, so line 312's guard is false: PI_1 is never compared and never cancelled. Execution falls to line 370 and creates PI_2 with a key that includes `replacingPi = PI_1`, so it is a NEW key and Stripe genuinely creates a second intent. Line 397's upsert (onConflict booking_id) then rewrites the single payments row to {PI_2, 'authorized'}. PI_2 has never been confirmed by any card, so it sits at `requires_payment_method`. PI_1 — the real hold — is now referenced by nothing in the database.
money_impact: The earner works and is never paid. At verify time `stripe-capture-payment` (line 89) looks the booking up by the payments row, finds PI_2, and calls `paymentIntents.capture(PI_2)` on an unconfirmed intent — it errors, `guard_bookings_write` refuses completed→verified without a `captured` payments row (20260730140000_pin_booking_insert_columns.sql:136-138), and the booking is permanently stuck. PI_1 lapses on Stripe's ~7-day timer and silently refunds the poster. Nothing reconciles it: `reconcile-stripe` iterates only over rows in `payments` (index.ts:69-88) and never enumerates Stripe's PaymentIntent list, so a PI whose id was overwritten out of the row is unreachable by the one control designed to catch DB-vs-Stripe divergence. In the milder variant (PI_1 was authorized but the booking not yet confirmed) the poster simply carries two simultaneous authorizations for the same gig on their card for up to 7 days.
fix_sketch: Distinguish `resource_missing` (PI genuinely gone → safe to recreate) from every other retrieve error. On any non-`resource_missing` failure, fail closed: return 503 and let the caller retry, rather than creating a second intent. Additionally, never overwrite `payments.payment_intent_id` while the prior intent's disposition is unknown — write the new intent only after the old one is confirmed cancelled or confirmed absent.
verifier_note: Three of the finding's load-bearing claims are wrong. (1) "Invisible to every control" is false: reconcile-stripe/index.ts:182 raises a CRITICAL `hold_dead_at_stripe` finding for exactly `p.status === 'authorized'` with `pi.status === 'requires_payment_method'` — which is precisely the state the orphan leaves behind — and controls_sweep_and_page dispatches reconcile-stripe hourly (20260806330000_dispatch_timeouts.sql:55). (2) "Permanently stuck" is false: `requires_payment_method` is IN `liveStatuses` (:311), so the very next createPaymentIntent call retrieves PI_2, matches the amount, and hands back PI_2's client secret; paying it produces a capturable hold and the booking settles normally. (3) The confirmed-booking variant needs a stale client or a hand-rolled call — web only opens AcceptPaymentModal from `b.status === "pending"` (hiring/page.tsx:325-327) and mobile only renders Accept under `status === 'pending'` (GigsScreen.js:776-778); `canHold` permits it but no UI drives it. The residue that IS real and undetected: PI_1 remains a live `requires_capture` authorization that the app can no longer cancel (stripe-cancel-payment only cancels the id stored in the row), so the poster's funds are double-held until Stripe's ~7-day expiry, and if the booking is then declined the row is marked cancelled and even reconcile check #5 stops firing. No money is created or destroyed and no one is charged twice; the harm is a temporary duplicate hold on the poster's card plus an operator page.

title: accept-booking resurrects a cancelled hold: it writes `payments.status='authorized'` with no status predicate and confirms the booking off a stale PaymentIntent read
summary: `accept-booking` reads the PaymentIntent status, then performs two unguarded writes. The payments write has no `.eq('status', …)` predicate (unlike the equivalent write in admin-payment-action/index.ts:94), so it overwrites a row that `stripe-cancel-payment` just marked `cancelled` back to `authorized`. Because `stripe-cancel-payment` explicitly permits voiding a hold on a `pending` booking, the poster can drive both endpoints concurrently and land a booking in `confirmed` with a cancelled PaymentIntent behind it and a ledger row that claims the hold is live.
trigger: Poster P owns job J; earner E's booking B is `pending`; P has already placed a hold via stripe-create-payment-intent and authorized the card, so PI is `requires_capture` and `payments` = {PI, 'authorized'}. P fires two concurrent requests with their own JWT: (1) POST accept-booking{B} — it reads the booking as `pending` (:44-54), reads the payments row (:57), and issues `paymentIntents.retrieve` (:65), which returns `requires_capture`; (2) POST stripe-cancel-payment{B} — every guard passes because `booking.status === 'pending'` is in `CANCELLABLE_STATUSES` (stripe-cancel-payment/index.ts:67), `started_at` is null, and the payment is `authorized`; it cancels the PI at Stripe and sets the row to `cancelled`. If (2) completes between (1)'s retrieve and (1)'s writes, accept-booking then executes `payments.update({status:'authorized'})` with no predicate, erasing the cancel, and `bookings.update({status:'confirmed'}).eq('status','pending')` succeeds because the earner-withdraw predicate at :82 only guards against a booking-status change, which the cancel path never made. Failed attempts cost the poster nothing and are infinitely repeatable: on a miss, accept-booking returns 409 HOLD_NOT_AUTHORIZED, the booking is still `pending` with a `cancelled` payment, so `isRecovery` is true and `canHold` permits a fresh hold (stripe-create-payment-intent:98-100) — re-authorize the card and try again.
money_impact: The earner performs the work for nothing. Post-race the booking reads `confirmed`, `JobsContext.acceptBooking` pushes "Booking accepted!" to the earner, and the gig shows Active on both sides — while Stripe holds $0. Neither client reads the payments table, so nothing surfaces the discrepancy to either party. At verify time `stripe-capture-payment` returns HOLD_EXPIRED (index.ts:98-103) and the booking can never reach `verified`. This is exactly the free-work scenario stripe-cancel-payment's own header comment (:54-66) claims CANCELLABLE_STATUSES closed; it closed the sequential form and left the concurrent one open, because accept-booking's check-then-act is not atomic and its write is unconditional.
fix_sketch: Guard the payments write with the status it was read at (`.eq('status', payment.status)`), check the affected-row count, and re-retrieve the PaymentIntent AFTER the booking flips to `confirmed` — rolling the booking back to `pending` if it is no longer `requires_capture`. Alternatively remove `pending` from stripe-cancel-payment's CANCELLABLE_STATUSES and require the caller to move the booking to `declined`/`cancelled` first, so no state exists in which a live hold is voidable while accept-booking considers the booking acceptable.
verifier_note: The mechanism is misattributed. The missing `.eq('status', …)` on accept-booking's payments write is the NARROWER of two orderings, and it is the more detectable one: it leaves status='authorized' with cancelled_at set against a canceled PI, which reconcile-stripe check #5 (index.ts:182) flags CRITICAL within the hour, and ctl_escrow_hold_lapsed_uncancelled fires at 8 days because it keys off greatest(created_at, cancelled_at). The wider and easier ordering is stripe-cancel-payment's OWN check-then-act: it reads booking.status at :32-36, passes CANCELLABLE_STATUSES, then makes a Stripe round-trip at :99 before writing — so if accept-booking completes anywhere inside that window it voids a live hold on a now-confirmed booking. That variant leaves payments='cancelled', which is honest and therefore invisible: reconcile check #5 requires status='authorized', ctl_settled_without_captured_payment only fires when the payments row is missing entirely (20260806040000:249-251), and ctl_money_exposed_on_dead_booking only covers declined/cancelled bookings. A fix that only adds the predicate to accept-booking's payments write leaves the worse ordering open; stripe-cancel-payment must re-assert the booking status atomically (or after the Stripe cancel, rolling back) as well.

title: Poster discounts are charged but never disclosed: the accept UI shows the pre-discount gig amount as the hold, and the edge response's three money fields do not reconcile
summary: The function authorizes `authorizedCents = amountCents - discountCents` (line 248) but returns only `amountCents`, `earnerAmountCents` and `feeCents` — never the discount or the amount actually authorized. Both clients therefore state the wrong hold amount at the moment of consent, and the three returned fields no longer satisfy `amountCents === earnerAmountCents + feeCents` once a poster discount applies.
trigger: An active `poster_discount` promotion (supabase/migrations/20260806110000_poster_discounts.sql, still live per 20260806340000) grants poster P a discount; `pin_booking_amount` stamps `bookings.poster_discount_cents` at INSERT (20260806320000_discount_headroom_after_credit.sql:141-225) and `consume_poster_discount` debits the campaign budget and writes a `promo_redemptions` row. P accepts a $100 gig on web. `stripe-create-payment-intent` computes `authorizedCents = 10000 - 155 = 9845` and creates the PaymentIntent for 9845, but returns `amountCents: 10000`. `AcceptPaymentModal` reads `res.amountCents` (:54) and renders "Hold $100.00 & accept" (:168 / :221) plus "$100.00 is held securely" (:101). Stripe's `PaymentElement`/`confirmCardPayment` display no amount of their own, so on web the button text is the ONLY amount the poster ever sees before authorizing. Mobile has the same defect in the post-authorization receipt: `GigsScreen.js:209,218` builds "$X held in escrow" from the same `amountCents`. Neither client reads `poster_discount_cents` anywhere — grep across src/ and web/lib returns zero hits.
money_impact: Every poster-discount redemption is invisible to its beneficiary. The campaign's `budget_cents` and `redemptions_used` are debited and `promo_redemptions` records a delivered benefit, while the poster is shown the undiscounted price and told that amount is held — so the discount buys zero perceived value and the marketing spend is destroyed. It is also a disclosure defect in the strict sense: the number displayed at the point of consent (and in the confirmation receipt) differs from the amount actually authorized on the card, and the poster's statement will not match what the app told them. The returned triple additionally fails to reconcile — `amountCents (10000) !== earnerAmountCents (9500) + feeCents (345)` — so any future client that renders the breakdown will show a $155 hole it cannot explain.
evidence: supabase/functions/stripe-create-payment-intent/index.ts:248 — `const authorizedCents = Math.max(50, amountCents - discountCents);` :370-376 — `stripe.paymentIntents.create({ amount: authorizedCents, … application_fee_amount: feeCents, … })` with the comment "The poster is charged the DISCOUNTED total, not the gig price." :434-442 — the response body is `{ clientSecret, customerId, ephemeralKey, amountCents, earnerAmountCents, feeCents, savedCard }` — `authorizedCents` and `discountCents` are never returned. web/components/AcceptPaymentModal.tsx:54 — `setAmountCents(res.amountCents ?? res.amount ?? 0);` :168 — `Hold {money(amountCents, { cents: true })} & accept` :221 — same string in `PayForm` :101 — `{money(amountCents,{cents:true})} is held securely for “{jobTitle}”` src/screens/GigsScreen.js:170,209,218 — `const { … amountCents } = await createPaymentIntent(bookingId); … const dollars = (amountCents / 100).toFixed(2); … \`$${dollars} held in escrow.\`` web/app/(app)/hiring/page.tsx:76-84 — `verifyHeldCents` returns `verifyBooking.amountCentsQuoted`, again pre-discount, and is passed to CompletionModal as `heldCents` (:464).
fix_sketch: Return `authorizedCents` (and `discountCents`) from the edge function and have both clients render the hold from `authorizedCents`, showing the discount as an explicit line ("$100.00 gig − $1.55 promo = $98.45 held"). Expose `poster_discount_cents` on the booking transform so `verifyHeldCents` can subtract it too. Keep `amountCents` as the gig value for the earner-facing split, but never label it as the amount held.
verifier_note: Two of the finding's claims are wrong or overstated. (a) "Neither client reads poster_discount_cents anywhere — grep returns zero hits" is factually false: src/lib/payments.js:100 maps it to `discountCents` and PaymentsScreen.js:313,423 renders it as a "Discount − $x" line in both the per-payment detail and the year summary, so the beneficiary does see it, just after the fact rather than at consent. (b) The three-field non-reconciliation is by design, not a hole: the asserted invariant in the function is `authorizedCents === earnerAmountCents + platformFeeCents` (:254), and `amountCents` is deliberately the gig value used for the earner-facing split (the earner's payout is genuinely unaffected by a poster discount). No current client renders the breakdown, so the "$155 hole" is hypothetical. Crucially, the error direction is in the poster's favour — they are charged LESS than the number displayed — so nobody is charged an amount they did not agree to. The only substantive residues are that the discount buys no perceived value at the moment it matters, and that the partial-capture ("report a problem") figure the poster sees is derived from the pre-discount heldCents while stripe-capture-payment computes `round(payment.amount_cents * pct)` off the discounted authorization (:167), a sub-dollar mismatch on a disputed gig.

title: Capture's promo settle-back refunds a poster discount in full, so budget_cents stops bounding poster_discount campaigns
summary: settle_booking_benefits values EVERY redemption on the booking with promo_benefit_cents(amount, r.fee_bps) — a fee-RATE differential. For a kind='poster_discount' redemption the stored fee_bps is the booking's own pinned rate, so the differential is 0 and `actual` settles to 0 while reserved_cents holds the flat discount that was genuinely delivered. delta = -reserved_cents, so promotions.spent_cents is credited back the entire discount at capture. The budget is therefore released on every successfully captured booking and only ever constrains concurrently-in-flight bookings, never lifetime spend.
trigger:
Promotion P: kind='poster_discount', poster_discount_cents=1000 ($10), budget_cents=50000, max_redemptions=100, max_benefit_cents=15000, status='active'. Standing rate 1000 bps, no fee-override grant anywhere. Poster holds a grant on P; earner books a $200 gig.
1) pin_booking_amount → consume_poster_discount: cap = poster_discount_headroom(20000,1000) = platform_fee_cents(20000,1000)=2000 minus floor(ceil(580)+30+25=635) = 1365; hit = least(1000, 1365, 15000) = 1000. It INSERTs promo_redemptions(fee_bps = p_fee_bps = 1000, reserved_cents = 1000) and does promotions.spent_cents += 1000. bookings/payments.poster_discount_cents = 1000.
2) stripe-create-payment-intent: authorizedCents = 20000-1000 = 19000, application_fee_amount = 2000-1000 = 1000. The discount is real: platform margin drops from 2000c to 1000c.
3) Poster verifies → stripe-capture-payment full branch: gigAmountCents = 19000 + 1000 = 20000, then rpc settle_booking_benefits(booking, 20000).
4) In settle: r.fee_bps = 1000 and fee_bps_at(now()) = 1000, so promo_benefit_cents(20000, 1000) = platform_fee_cents(20000,1000) - platform_fee_cents(20000,1000) = 0. actual = least(15000, 0) = 0. delta = 0 - 1000 = -1000. promotions.spent_cents goes back to 0; promo_redemptions.benefit_cents = 0, settled = true, settled_at = now().
Repeat 100 times: redemptions_used reaches 100 (that IS still enforced), but spent_cents never exceeds one in-flight reserve, so the `spent_cents + hit <= budget_cents` increment-is-the-check in consume_poster_discount never binds.
money_impact: The stated design property — 'loss is bounded by construction: budget_cents + max_redemptions' — is false for the entire poster_discount kind. Lifetime spend becomes max_redemptions x discount instead of budget_cents. On the SHIPPED preset 'first_hire_discount' (budget_dollars 500, max_redemptions 100, discount_dollars 10, admin/app/(console)/promotions/presets.ts) the platform can pay out up to $1,000 of margin against a $500 budget — 2x overrun, and more on higher-value gigs where the headroom clamp does not bite. Compounding it, the /promotions budget burn-down reads ~$0 spent for the campaign's whole life, so an operator watching the one number that is supposed to bound the giveaway sees no spend at all. No control catches it: ctl_discount_charged_not_delivered needs reserved_cents > delivered (they are equal), and ctl_benefit_never_settled needs settled_at null (it is set).

fix_sketch: Branch on the promotion kind inside settle_booking_benefits: for kind='poster_discount' the true cost is the discount actually delivered — least(reserved_cents, bookings.poster_discount_cents) — not promo_benefit_cents. Keep promo_benefit_cents for kind='fee_override' only. Also add a control asserting that, for every settled poster_discount redemption, benefit_cents equals bookings.poster_discount_cents.
verifier_note: Two overstatements to fix, neither fatal to the finding. (a) Lifetime loss is NOT unbounded — settle never decrements promotions.redemptions_used (only release_booking_benefits does), so max_redemptions still binds; the exposure is max_redemptions × min(poster_discount_cents, per-gig headroom), which on the shipped preset is $1,000 against a $500 budget only for gigs ≳$149 (below that the headroom clamp bites first). (b) The 'settles to 0' arithmetic holds only when fee_bps_quoted equals the standing rate. If the earner sits on a loyalty tier (tier_fee_bps, 20260806120000:74) or holds a fee_override, fee_bps_quoted is lower and the poster_discount redemption settles to the EARNER's rate differential — a number with no relation to the discount, which can land above or below the reserve. So the defect is better stated as 'settle values a flat-cent benefit with a rate-differential formula', of which settle-to-zero is the common case. Also note benefit_cents has no readers anywhere in the repo (grep), so the only material consequence is spent_cents and the /promotions burn-down that renders it (admin/app/(console)/promotions/page.tsx:95).

title: The dispute-recording branch is gated on the REQUESTED pct, not on whether a partial capture happened — a poster can file a false '50% paid' dispute on a fully settled booking
summary: The `if (capturePctFinal < 1)` block that inserts the disputes row sits OUTSIDE the `if (payment.status !== 'captured')` capture block, and the booking status gate accepts 'verified'. So on a booking that has already been captured at 100% and verified, a second call with pct<1 skips all money movement but still inserts an open disputes row recording pct_paid = 50. The write is not conditioned on capturedGigCents !== null (the flag that actually says a capture ran), which is the same signal the settle call two blocks above correctly uses.
trigger:
1) Poster verifies normally: stripe-capture-payment runs the full branch, payments.status='captured', bookings.status='verified', earner credited 100%.
2) Same poster POSTs to stripe-capture-payment again with {bookingId, pct: 0.5, disputeReason: 'work was poor'} using their own session token. Gates passed: job.poster_id === user.id (true), booking.status is 'verified' (in the allow-list at :81), payment.status === 'captured' so both the payouts re-check and the whole capture block at :129 are skipped, capturedGigCents stays null so settle is skipped, credit_earnings is a no-op.
3) Line 255 `if (capturePctFinal < 1)` is still true → no existing dispute row → INSERT disputes(booking_id, raised_by=poster, pct_paid=50, reason, photos). disputes.status defaults to open.
The same call works on any booking the poster owns that reached 'completed'/'verified', including one settled by earner-claim-payment.
money_impact: Two concrete harms. (a) A third party loses vested money: vest_bonuses only promotes a referral bonus pending→payable when `not exists (select 1 from disputes d where d.booking_id = b.source_booking_id and coalesce(d.status,'open') in ('open','investigating'))`. The bonus row stays 'pending' at every hourly sweep for as long as the fabricated dispute is open, so the REFERRER (who is not a party to this booking and cannot see or contest the dispute) is permanently denied their bonus until an admin resolves a dispute about a payment that was never reduced. (b) The disputes row is the audit record support and the earner both read (admin /disputes and /bookings/[id] render `{pct_paid}% paid`); it now asserts the earner was paid 50% of a charge that was captured and transferred at 100%, which is exactly the evidence an operator would act on when deciding a refund via admin-payment-action (reverse_transfer:true pulls the money back out of the earner's connected account).
fix_sketch: Record the dispute only when this invocation actually performed a reduced capture: change the guard to `if (capturedGigCents !== null && capturePctFinal < 1)`, and/or move the insert inside the partial branch immediately after the successful stripe.paymentIntents.capture. Independently, reject the request up front when payment.status === 'captured' && wantsPartial (409 'already settled at full amount') rather than silently ignoring the pct.
verifier_note: Trim two claims. (a) The fabricated row cannot block the target booking's payout — earner-claim-payment's dispute gate (index.ts:167-172) is moot on a booking already captured and verified, so the 'permanent payout block' this reopens is only the referral-bonus one, plus the audit-record corruption. (b) The admin-refund path is a human decision, not an automatic consequence: the row misleads an operator reading `{pct_paid}% paid` at admin/app/(console)/bookings/[id]/page.tsx:26, it does not itself move money. Net harm: an indefinitely-held third-party bonus and a false money record in the only server-authored dispute log, obtainable by any poster with a session token and no money at stake.

title: Two concurrent captures with different pct race the pre-capture split write, crediting the earner the full net when only a partial amount was captured
summary: Both branches persist the computed split to payments BEFORE calling Stripe, with a plain UPDATE and no row lock, no conditional predicate, and no capture-side idempotency key. Two concurrent invocations both observe status='authorized', both write their split, and whichever capture wins at Stripe leaves the row holding the OTHER call's numbers. credit_earnings then reads earner_amount_cents off that row, so the earner's ledger can be credited the full net against a 50% capture.
trigger:
Poster fires two requests to stripe-capture-payment for the same bookingId at the same time: R2 with {pct: 0.5, disputeReason:'x'} and R1 with no pct. Both read payment.status='authorized' at :100 and both enter the capture block at :129.
Interleaving: R2 writes {fee_cents: 173, earner_amount_cents: 4827} (:187). R1 writes {fee_cents: 1000, earner_amount_cents: 9000} (:208). R2 calls paymentIntents.capture(amount_to_capture: 5000, application_fee_amount: 173) → succeeds. R1 calls paymentIntents.capture() → Stripe returns payment_intent_unexpected_state → R1 throws to the terminal catch and returns 500 without ever writing status. R2 writes status='captured' (:195), then calls credit_earnings, which reads earner_amount_cents = 9000 (R1's value) and credits the earner $90.
Stripe actually captured $50 and transferred $48.27.
money_impact: profiles.earnings_today/week/total are credited ~$90 against $48.27 actually transferred, and the earnings_credited flag is now consumed so no retry corrects it. payments.fee_cents/earner_amount_cents disagree with the charge, which corrupts the two places that derive from them: admin-payment-action computes its refundable ceiling as `capturedCents = earner_amount_cents + fee_cents` (so the console offers to refund $100 on a $50 charge — Stripe rejects, surfacing as a 500 rather than a clear message), and the Tax Center's year income figure overstates the earner's 1099 income. The pre-capture write is deliberate (a fast webhook must not read a stale value) but nothing serialises two writers, and the external Stripe reconciliation control is what would eventually flag it — detection after the fact, not prevention.
fix_sketch: Claim the capture before doing anything: `update payments set status='capturing' where id=$1 and status='authorized' returning *` and bail with 409 when it returns no row, so only one invocation can proceed. Pass an idempotencyKey to stripe.paymentIntents.capture built from payment_intent_id + captureCents + feeCents. Make the pre-capture split write conditional (`.eq('status','authorized')`), and after a successful capture reconcile earner_amount_cents/fee_cents from the returned PaymentIntent's amount_received and latest_charge.application_fee_amount — the same Stripe-is-the-authority discipline earner-claim-payment already applies.
verifier_note: Downgrade the practical exposure, not the mechanism. The trigger is adversarial-only and unprofitable: it requires the poster to fire two simultaneous requests with DIFFERENT pct on the same booking (a double-tap or client retry sends identical pct, and both writers then write identical numbers — no desync). The interleaving also has no attacker payoff: the real money at Stripe is whichever capture won, and the corruption lands in profiles.earnings_* and payments.fee_cents/earner_amount_cents. The symmetric ordering (full capture wins, partial split persists) UNDER-credits the earner, which is the likelier complaint. Note the neighbouring path is already immune by a different discipline — earner-claim-payment reconciles earner_amount_cents from Stripe's amount_received and latest_charge.application_fee_amount after capture (index.ts:232-290) precisely because of this race, which is the pattern the fix sketch correctly proposes porting here.

title: Both claim time-gates read payments.created_at, which a recovery re-hold never updates — every re-held booking is claimable in full the instant the poster places the new hold
summary: holdPlacedAt and the belt-and-suspenders grace check both derive from payments.created_at, which records the FIRST authorization. stripe-create-payment-intent's recovery re-hold upsert deliberately leaves created_at at the original hold and writes the fresh timestamp to payments.authorized_at instead. So on any re-held booking both the `holdNearlyExpired` second anchor and the `Date.now() < created_at + GRACE_MS` backstop evaluate against a timestamp that is by construction 7+ days old, and the earner can capture 100% of a hold that is seconds old.
trigger: Day 0: poster accepts a gig; payments row is created (created_at = Day 0, status 'authorized'). Day 7: Stripe auto-cancels the uncaptured authorization; stripe-webhook's payment_intent.canceled handler sets status='cancelled' and deliberately leaves a confirmed/earner_done booking at 'confirmed' (index.ts:200-226). Day 8: the poster re-places the hold — stripe-create-payment-intent allows it (isRecovery, canHold) and upserts payment_intent_id/status/authorized_at, leaving created_at = Day 0. Day 8 + 1 second: the earner calls earner-claim-payment. slot.starts_at is in the past so scheduledTimePassed = true; holdPlacedAt = Day 0 so holdNearlyExpired = Day 8 >= Day 0 + 6d = true; claimUnlocked = true. The belt-and-suspenders check `Date.now() < created_at + GRACE_MS` is Day 8 < Day 3 = false, so it passes too. The function captures the FULL hold, credits the earner, and forces the booking to 'verified'. A second, equally concrete trigger: the poster's first accept fails (webhook payment_intent.payment_failed sets status='failed', created_at pinned at that first attempt) and the poster retries days later — the fresh hold is then claimable the moment the slot's start time passes.
money_impact: The poster is charged the full authorized amount with zero window to verify, to run the partial-capture/dispute path (stripe-capture-payment's 50%-floor remedy), or to cancel — on a booking whose work is asserted only by the earner's own earner_done flag. The re-hold is exactly the flow stripe-capture-payment tells the poster to use ('Re-confirm this booking to place a new hold, then verify again', index.ts:101), so the poster is walked into it. The intended minimum protection is 3 days between hold placement and claim; on a re-hold it is zero seconds. The earner gets amount - fee; the poster loses the entire disputed amount.
evidence:
earner-claim-payment/index.ts:111-115 `const { data: holdRow } = await supabase.from('payments').select('created_at')...; const payment_created_at_hint = holdRow?.created_at ? new Date(holdRow.created_at).getTime() : null;`
earner-claim-payment/index.ts:142-148 `const holdPlacedAt = payment_created_at_hint; const holdNearlyExpired = holdPlacedAt !== null && Date.now() >= holdPlacedAt + (HOLD_LIFETIME_MS - HOLD_EXPIRY_MARGIN_MS); ... const claimUnlocked = Date.now() >= eligibleAt.getTime() || (scheduledTimePassed && holdNearlyExpired);`
earner-claim-payment/index.ts:193-201 `// Belt-and-suspenders: ... a hold placed moments ago can never be instantly claimed.` then `if (!payment.created_at || Date.now() < new Date(payment.created_at).getTime() + GRACE_MS)`
stripe-create-payment-intent/index.ts:406-411 `// When THIS hold was placed. created_at keeps recording the first one ... a recovery re-hold updates this and leaves that history intact.` / `authorized_at: new Date().toISOString(),` (upsert onConflict 'booking_id' — created_at is not in the payload)
supabase/migrations/20260806150000_authorized_at.sql:4-25 states the exact defect ('Neither column records the current hold on a RECOVERY re-hold') and 20260806150000:56,62,78,85 switch ctl_escrow_hold_lapsed_uncancelled and ctl_escrow_hold_expiring_work_done to `coalesce(p.authorized_at, ...)`. `grep -rn authorized_at supabase/functions/` returns only stripe-create-payment-intent:410 — the money gate was never migrated. git log confirms earner-claim-payment was last touched in 2972075, AFTER the authorized_at migration landed in e5784dc.
fix_sketch: Select `authorized_at, created_at` from payments and use `coalesce(authorized_at, created_at)` for BOTH holdPlacedAt and the belt-and-suspenders grace check, matching the two controls the same migration fixed. The slot-time anchor (eligibleAt) stays as-is.
verifier_note: Two corrections to the mechanism and one to the reach. (1) The `holdNearlyExpired` second anchor is not the load-bearing part: on any re-held booking the slot-based `eligibleAt` (slot + 3 days) has essentially always already passed, so claimUnlocked is true regardless. The ONLY protection the poster loses is the belt-and-suspenders grace check at :196 — that is the single line the bug disables, and it is the single line worth fixing. (2) The 'completed' recovery re-hold described in the trigger is not reachable from any shipped client: `rg -n HOLD_EXPIRED src/ web/ admin/` returns nothing, so no UI handles stripe-capture-payment's 'Re-confirm this booking' instruction and no screen calls createPaymentIntent on a completed booking (GigsScreen only exposes it via handleAccept on a pending request). The reachable variants are the webhook-demoted 'pending' re-accept above and the payment_failed retry, both of which go through the normal Accept button. (3) Impact: no money is created or destroyed and the amount captured is the pinned, agreed amount_cents_quoted for a booking whose slot has passed and which the earner flagged done. What is lost is the poster's 3-day window to run stripe-capture-payment's partial remedy (floored at 50%, so at most half the amount is at stake) or to file a booking-scoped report/dispute that arms the fail-closed gates. Fix as proposed — coalesce(authorized_at, created_at) for the :196 check — matching the two controls the same migration corrected.

title: A poster's no-show report filed from the earner's profile carries no booking_id, so the fail-closed UNDER_REVIEW gate never sees it
summary: The report gate is scoped `.eq('booking_id', bookingId)`, but the app's primary 'report this user' flows (PublicProfileScreen on mobile, /u/[id] on web, and JobDetail) call submitReport with no bookingId, so reports.booking_id is NULL. Only the in-chat report path sets it. The reason list offered on those screens includes 'No-show / did not complete' — the exact scenario the gate exists to block — and a report filed that way is invisible to the claim. Combined with the removal of the disputes client-insert policy, the poster has no way at all to arm either fail-closed gate.
trigger: Poster posts a gig; earner books and the poster accepts (escrow hold placed). The earner never shows up but taps 'I'm on site' (guard_bookings_write's earner branch permits setting started_at once while status='confirmed', 20260730140000:164-166), which makes trg_guard_started_booking_cancel and stripe-cancel-payment both refuse to release the hold. The earner then marks done. The poster opens the earner's profile, taps Report, and picks 'No-show / did not complete' — submitReport is called with reportedUserId only, so booking_id is NULL. Three days after the slot time the earner calls earner-claim-payment: the reports count query filters on booking_id and returns 0, so UNDER_REVIEW does not fire; the disputes count is 0 because 20260726000000 dropped disputes_insert_party and no client can insert one. The full hold is captured and the booking is forced to 'verified'.
money_impact: The poster is charged the full gig amount for work that was never performed, after filing exactly the report the gate is designed to honour. The earner receives amount - fee into their Connect account. The poster's only remaining remedy is stripe-capture-payment with pct >= 0.5 (a hard 50% floor, index.ts:71) executed before the earner claims — i.e. they must actively pay at least half for a no-show, and only if they win the race.
evidence:
earner-claim-payment/index.ts:178-182 `const { count: reportCount, error: reportErr } = await supabase.from('reports').select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true }).eq('booking_id', bookingId).neq('source', 'auto').is('resolved_at', null); if (reportErr || (reportCount ?? 1) > 0) { return json({ error: 'UNDER_REVIEW', ... }, 409); }`
src/screens/PublicProfileScreen.js:126 `await submitReport({ reporterId: user.id, reportedUserId: userId, reason });`  (no bookingId)
web/app/(app)/u/[id]/page.tsx:194 `await submitReport({ reporterId: user.id, reportedUserId: id, reason: reportReason, details: reportDetails || null });`  (no bookingId)
src/screens/JobDetailScreen.js:175 `await submitReport({ reporterId: user.id, reportedUserId: job.posterId, jobId: job.id, reason });`  (no bookingId)
src/lib/moderation.js:59 `'No-show / did not complete',` — offered on those same screens
src/lib/moderation.js:63-72 submitReport defaults `bookingId = null` and inserts it verbatim; supabase/migration_trial_p0.sql:12 `booking_id uuid references public.bookings(id) on delete set null` (nullable)
supabase/migrations/20260726000000_protect_earner_settlement_anchor.sql:109 `drop policy if exists "disputes_insert_party" on public.disputes;` — never re-created in any later migration
fix_sketch: Widen the gate to also count unresolved user reports where reported_user_id = booking.earner_id and (booking_id = bookingId OR job_id = booking.job_id OR created_at >= booking.created_at), i.e. any open report by the poster against this earner touching this engagement. Cheaper alternative: make the poster-facing report entry points pass bookingId when a booking connects the two users (the data is already in JobsContext.posterBookings).
verifier_note: Real but narrow and mis-severitised. Accurate statement: three report entry points (mobile PublicProfile, web /u/[id], mobile JobDetail) drop the booking association, so a report filed there is invisible to a gate that is deliberately booking-scoped; the booking-scoped in-chat report path works and is the intended arming mechanism. Take only the cheap half of the proposed fix — have those screens pass bookingId when a booking connects the two users (the data is already in JobsContext.posterBookings) — and explicitly reject the server-side widening, which would restore the permanent-payout-block attack the settlement-anchor migration was written to eliminate.

title: The claim path never calls settle_booking_benefits, so a promo redemption on a self-settled booking stays reserved at the worst case forever
summary: consume_promo_grant charges a campaign the worst-case benefit at booking INSERT and stripe-capture-payment gives the difference back after capture via settle_booking_benefits. earner-claim-payment captures, credits, and drives the booking to 'verified' without ever calling it, and no DB trigger covers the gap (trg_zz_release_benefits fires only on 'declined'/'cancelled') and stripe-webhook's payment_intent.succeeded handler does not call it either.
trigger: An earner redeems a fee-override promo code, then books a gig (pin_booking_amount -> consume_promo_grant reserves the worst-case benefit against promotions.budget_cents and inserts a promo_redemptions row with released_at and settled_at both NULL). The poster accepts, ghosts, and the earner self-settles through earner-claim-payment. The function sets bookings.status = 'verified' at index.ts:300-302 and returns. promo_redemptions.settled_at stays NULL forever with the booking in a terminal state — which is exactly the predicate of ctl_benefit_never_settled, so the hourly control sweep files a 'high'/'money' finding on every such booking and it can never auto-resolve.
money_impact: The campaign's spent_cents permanently holds the worst-case reserve instead of the real benefit, so budget_cents and max_redemptions are consumed faster than money was actually given away. The campaign exhausts early and later users are silently denied a benefit that was budgeted for them (consume_promo_grant's increment-is-the-check refuses once spent_cents + hit > budget_cents). It also guarantees a permanently-open high-severity control finding per affected booking, which is the false-positive shape 20260806150000 explicitly warns teaches operators to ignore the queue.
evidence:
earner-claim-payment/index.ts:291-302 — `await supabase.rpc('credit_earnings', ...)` is followed directly by the bookings update to 'verified'; there is no settle_booking_benefits call anywhere in the file (`grep -n settle_booking_benefits supabase/functions/earner-claim-payment/index.ts` -> no match).
stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:240-250 `if (capturedGigCents !== null) { const { error: settleErr } = await supabase.rpc('settle_booking_benefits', { p_booking: bookingId, p_amount_cents: capturedGigCents }); ... }`
supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:212-224 `if new.status in ('declined', 'cancelled') ... perform public.release_booking_benefits(...)` — 'verified' is not covered.
supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:309-315 ctl_benefit_never_settled: `where r.released_at is null and r.settled_at is null and b.status in ('verified','declined','cancelled') and r.created_at < now() - interval '2 hours'`
supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts:142-153 — the payment_intent.succeeded handler updates status and calls credit_earnings only.
fix_sketch: After credit_earnings, mirror stripe-capture-payment: `await supabase.rpc('settle_booking_benefits', { p_booking: bookingId, p_amount_cents: capturedCents + poster_discount_cents })`, non-fatal and logged on error, using the same immutable inputs the fee was derived from.
verifier_note: Directionally right, impact overstated by roughly an order of magnitude. The residual money delta is zero for a full capture; the only case where reserve and true cost diverge is a change in the standing rate between booking and claim, because promo_benefit_cents measures the counterfactual at fee_bps_at(now()) — and that can go either way and is bounded by max_benefit_cents. The genuine consequences are (a) a permanently-open 'high'/'money' ctl_benefit_never_settled finding per self-settled booking, i.e. exactly the alert-fatigue false positive the control framework warns about, and (b) promo_redemptions.benefit_cents/settled staying wrong forever in campaign reporting. The suggested fix and its p_amount_cents basis (capturedCents + poster_discount_cents, mirroring stripe-capture-payment's capturedGigCents) are correct; it should be non-fatal and logged, as at the existing call site.

title: A stale or retried payment_intent.payment_failed kills a LIVE escrow hold: 'authorized' is in the allow-list, so the row is stamped 'failed' and the confirmed booking is demoted to 'pending'
summary: The payment_failed handler's status precondition is `.in('status', ['pending','authorized'])`. 'authorized' is the exact state a genuinely live, verified `requires_capture` hold sits in — accept-booking writes that literal value (accept-booking/index.ts:75) after retrieving the PI from Stripe and confirming `pi.status === 'requires_capture'`. The payments row therefore cannot distinguish "optimistically authorized, not yet confirmed by the poster" (written by stripe-create-payment-intent:405 before the client confirms) from "real hold verified live at Stripe", so this guard cannot be correct as written. Any payment_failed event that arrives after acceptance clobbers a real hold to 'failed', and then unconditionally re-reads the booking and demotes confirmed -> pending. Both settlement paths hard-refuse a 'failed' row, so the money can never be captured even though Stripe is still holding it.
trigger: No exotic ordering needed — the handler's own 500 path (index.ts:374-378) is sufficient. (1) Poster's first PaymentSheet confirmation is declined -> Stripe emits payment_intent.payment_failed for PI-A. (2) The webhook run throws on a transient supabase-js fetch failure at index.ts:169 or 183 (after the payments UPDATE at 165-168 has already been applied) -> returns 500 -> Stripe queues redelivery, retrying for ~3 days. (3) The poster retries the same PaymentIntent with a second card, it authorizes, they tap Accept; accept-booking verifies pi.status === 'requires_capture' and writes payments.status='authorized', bookings.status='confirmed'. (4) Stripe redelivers the queued payment_failed. `.in('status',['pending','authorized'])` now MATCHES the live row -> status='failed'; booking is 'confirmed' with earner_done=false -> demoted to 'pending'. The same clobber is reachable without any 500 purely from Stripe's documented lack of ordering guarantees between payment_failed and the later authorization. Nothing recovers: no path ever writes 'authorized' back onto a 'failed' row.
money_impact: The earner works and cannot be paid by any route. stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:98-103 returns HOLD_EXPIRED for status 'failed'; earner-claim-payment/index.ts:190-192 returns HOLD_EXPIRED for the same. Stripe still holds the full authorization and auto-releases it to the poster at ~7 days, so the poster receives the completed work for free and the earner is out the full gig value (e.g. $200 gig -> $180 net never paid). Worse, if the poster re-accepts: stripe-create-payment-intent:92 admits status 'failed' as re-holdable, :98 sets isRecovery, and the reconcile-and-cancel branch at :307 runs ONLY for `existingPay.status === 'authorized'` — so it is SKIPPED, PI-A is never cancelled, and a second PaymentIntent is created (the idempotency key at :385 includes replacingPi = PI-A's id, so it is a genuinely new intent). The poster now carries TWO simultaneous authorizations for one booking — 2x the amount they agreed to, held on their card until PI-A lapses. Detection is near-zero: reconcile-stripe's six checks all miss this shape (status 'failed' + amount_received 0 satisfies none of #1-#5), ctl_money_exposed_on_dead_booking requires booking status declined/cancelled, and ctl_stranded_pending_booking only fires 24h after the scheduled time has already passed.
evidence:
stripe-webhook/index.ts:165-168 — `await supabase.from('payments').update({ status: 'failed' }).eq('payment_intent_id', pi.id).in('status', ['pending', 'authorized']);`
stripe-webhook/index.ts:185-187 — `if (bk && ['pending', 'confirmed'].includes(bk.status) && !bk.earner_done) { await supabase.from('bookings').update({ status: 'pending' })... }` (this demotion is NOT gated on whether the payments UPDATE above actually matched a row)
accept-booking/index.ts:65-75 — `const pi = await stripe.paymentIntents.retrieve(...); if (pi.status !== 'requires_capture') return ...HOLD_NOT_AUTHORIZED...; await supabase.from('payments').update({ status: 'authorized' })` — the verified-live state is spelled with the SAME literal the guard admits.
stripe-create-payment-intent/index.ts:405 — `status: 'authorized',` written immediately after `paymentIntents.create`, before the client has confirmed anything.
stripe-create-payment-intent/index.ts:307 — `if (existingPay?.payment_intent_id && existingPay.status === 'authorized') {` — the orphan-hold reconciler is skipped for a 'failed' row.
stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:98 — `if (payment.status === 'cancelled' || payment.status === 'failed') { return json({ error: 'HOLD_EXPIRED' ... }, 409); }`
fix_sketch: Drop 'authorized' from the allow-list and re-derive truth from Stripe instead of from our own ambiguous column: in the payment_failed handler, retrieve the PaymentIntent and no-op unless `pi.status` is one of requires_payment_method/requires_confirmation/canceled (i.e. genuinely not holding funds). Separately, give the row a distinct state for a hold that accept-booking has verified live (e.g. 'authorized' only after verification, 'created' before it) so a precondition can be written that means what it says. Gate the booking demotion on the payments UPDATE having actually matched a row (`.select('id')` and check the count), and make stripe-create-payment-intent's orphan-hold reconciler run for every non-captured prior PI, not just status==='authorized'.
verifier_note:
Two claims in the finding are wrong and one is over-stated.
(1) "Nothing recovers: no path ever writes 'authorized' back onto a 'failed' row" is FALSE. stripe-create-payment-intent:92 explicitly admits status 'failed' as re-holdable, :98-100 permits a recovery re-hold even on a COMPLETED booking, and the upsert at :397-411 writes status:'authorized' back onto the same row (onConflict 'booking_id'). The accurate statement is that no CLIENT surfaces that path: `HOLD_EXPIRED` appears in zero files under src/, web/ or admin/, and GigsScreen's handleAccept is only reachable from a pending booking — so recovery is support-only in practice, not impossible.
(2) The clobber only bites when the retry stays on the SAME PaymentIntent. If the poster dismisses the sheet and re-runs createPaymentIntent, a new PI-B is minted (replacingPi changes the idempotency key) and the row's payment_intent_id is overwritten by the upsert — so the redelivered payment_failed's `.eq('payment_intent_id', PI-A)` matches zero rows, the `.single()` at :169-170 returns null, and BOTH the status clobber and the booking demotion no-op. The live path is specifically the in-sheet card retry.
(3) The trigger requires a genuine webhook delivery failure (non-2xx or timeout) on the payment_failed event — Stripe only redelivers what it failed to deliver. Pure out-of-order delivery within the ~20-60s a human takes to enter a second card is not a realistic mechanism, so the "same clobber is reachable without any 500" sentence should be dropped. That conjunction (card decline + delivery failure on that event + redelivery landing after acceptance) is what takes this off critical.
The double-authorization consequence is otherwise correct as written and is the sharpest part of the finding: :307 gates the orphan reconciler on `existingPay.status === 'authorized'`, so a 'failed' row skips it, PI-A is never cancelled, and the orphaned PI is invisible to reconcile-stripe (no payments row references it any more).

title: payment_intent.succeeded credits credit_earnings from the pre-computed split and never reconciles to pi.amount_received — the over-credit named in admin-payment-action's own header is still live
summary: The handler stamps the row 'captured' and calls credit_earnings, which credits whatever `payments.earner_amount_cents` happens to hold (20260722010000_audit_followups.sql:130-136 — the last definition of credit_earnings). Neither the handler nor the RPC ever looks at `pi.amount_received` or the charge's `application_fee_amount`. This is the only one of the three credit paths that does not reconcile against Stripe: earner-claim-payment/index.ts:232-290 explicitly retrieves the PI, reads amount_received and application_fee_amount, and rewrites earner_amount_cents BEFORE crediting, commenting "STRIPE is the sole source of truth for the amount — we NEVER pre-write a computed amount." The webhook does exactly what that comment forbids. admin-payment-action/index.ts:6-8 names the defect as the reason that function exists, but the remedy shipped was new console tools, not a reconcile in this handler — the over-credit is unchanged.
trigger: Two concrete sequences. (A) Stripe Dashboard partial capture: an operator captures $50 of a $200 hold in the Dashboard (the console has release_hold/refund/record_reversal but NO capture op, so the Dashboard is the only route). Stripe fires payment_intent.succeeded with amount_received=5000; the handler credits earner_amount_cents=18000, which stripe-create-payment-intent wrote at AUTHORIZATION time (:404). (B) Entirely in-app, no Dashboard access: poster captures at pct=0.6 -> partial branch writes earner_amount_cents=5400/fee=600 and captures 6000 at Stripe, but the HTTP response times out so the function throws at :191 and returns 500 with the row still status='authorized'. The poster retries from CompletionModal without reporting a problem (pct absent) before the webhook lands: the full branch at :199-217 recomputes earnerAmountCents = amount_cents - fullFee = 9000, PERSISTS it at :208-211, then `paymentIntents.capture` throws payment_intent_unexpected_state and the pre-write is never rolled back. The queued payment_intent.succeeded then credits 9000 against 6000 actually captured.
money_impact: Sequence (A): earner's earnings_today/week/total are credited $180 while Stripe transferred $45 (5000 captured minus the 500 application fee) — a $135 phantom credit on one booking. Sequence (B): $90 credited against $54 actually transferred — $36 phantom. profiles.earnings_* is the earner's dashboard, the Tax Center income figure and the year-end tax-summary CSV, so the worker is shown and files income they never received. Nothing ever reverses it: record_refund/debit_earnings is the only decrementer and it is driven by refunds, not by capture shortfalls. ctl_earnings_total_drift cannot catch it — it sums the same wrong earner_amount_cents from payments, so the ledger is internally self-consistent and the control passes. Only reconcile-stripe's check #1 (captured_total_mismatch, index.ts:115-120) sees it, and it merely files a control_findings row; it corrects nothing, and its window is `payments.created_at >= now()-14d` LIMIT 200, which a recovery re-hold (created_at is preserved by the upsert) can fall outside entirely.
evidence:
stripe-webhook/index.ts:144-152 — `await supabase.from('payments').update({ status: 'captured', captured_at: ... }).eq('payment_intent_id', pi.id); ... if (paid?.id) await supabase.rpc('credit_earnings', { p_payment_id: paid.id });` — `pi.amount_received` is never read anywhere in the file (zero occurrences).
supabase/migrations/20260722010000_audit_followups.sql:130-136 (FINAL definition of credit_earnings) — `update public.payments set earnings_credited = true where id = p_payment_id and ... status = 'captured' and coalesce(earner_amount_cents,0) > 0 returning earner_amount_cents into v_amount;`
admin-payment-action/index.ts:6-8 — "every remediation was \"open the Stripe Dashboard\" — which silently desynced the ledger, because a Dashboard capture fires payment_intent.succeeded and that handler credits the earner the full pre-computed split without reading amount_received."
earner-claim-payment/index.ts:237-290 — `const settled = await stripe.paymentIntents.retrieve(..., { expand: ['latest_charge'] }); const capturedCents = settled.amount_received ?? 0; ... update({ earner_amount_cents: capturedCents - feeCents, fee_cents: feeCents })` — the reconcile the webhook is missing.
stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:208-212 — the full-capture branch persists earnerAmountCents BEFORE `stripe.paymentIntents.capture()` and does not roll it back when that call throws.
fix_sketch: In the payment_intent.succeeded handler, reconcile before crediting exactly as earner-claim-payment does: retrieve the PI with `expand: ['latest_charge']`, and if `amount_received` (or the charge's application_fee_amount) disagrees with `earner_amount_cents + fee_cents` on the row, rewrite the row from Stripe's numbers first, then call credit_earnings. `event.data.object` already carries amount_received on the succeeded event, so the common case needs no extra API call — compare `pi.amount_received` to `earner_amount_cents + fee_cents` and only fetch the charge when they differ. Fail closed (leave the row uncredited and log fatal) rather than crediting a figure Stripe does not confirm.
verifier_note:
The impact is over-stated on two counts.
(1) The normal in-app paths are already defended, by design: BOTH capture branches persist fee_cents/earner_amount_cents BEFORE calling Stripe (:187-190 partial, :208-211 full) precisely so the webhook credits the right number. So the over-credit is not a property of the happy path — it needs either operator action outside the app (A) or a mid-flow partial-capture failure followed by a full-capture retry (B).
(2) "Only reconcile-stripe's check #1 sees it, and it merely files a control_findings row" understates the detector. reconcile-stripe check #1 (index.ts:115-120, TOLERANCE_CENTS = 0) fires on exactly this shape once the row is 'captured', and it is dispatched HOURLY from controls_sweep_and_page with days=14/limit=200 and a 120s pg_net timeout (20260806330000_dispatch_timeouts.sql:55-64), with auto-resolve when it clears. It is a working detector, not a theoretical one; it just does not self-correct. The remaining real gap is that the window is keyed on payments.created_at, which the recovery-re-hold upsert preserves — an over-credit on an old re-held payment can age out unexamined.
Also note scenario (B) is a purely ledger-side desync (profiles.earnings_*, Tax Center, the tax CSV); Stripe collected the correct partial amount, so no money left the platform — that is the difference between this and a capture-side defect.

title: payments.refund_source='admin' is sticky and permanently disarms charge.dispute.created for that booking — including the only control that detects an unledgered chargeback
summary: recordReversal early-returns for any payment whose `refund_source === 'admin'`, and that check sits in the SHARED helper — so it suppresses the disputes row for charge.dispute.created (a genuine customer chargeback) exactly as it does for charge.refunded (an admin remediation). admin-payment-action/index.ts:178 stamps refund_source='admin' on the payments row BEFORE calling Stripe and nothing ever clears it, so the suppression is permanent for the life of the booking. The suppression is not merely cosmetic: ctl_external_reversal_not_ledgered — the control built specifically to catch a chargeback the console never recorded — is a JOIN onto the very disputes rows recordReversal writes, so when no row is filed the detector produces nothing.
trigger: Ordinary sequence, no race. (1) A $100 booking is captured and the earner credited. (2) The poster complains; an admin issues a $10 goodwill partial refund via the console -> admin-payment-action:178 sets refund_source='admin' and it is never reset. (3) Weeks later the poster charges back the remaining $90. Stripe fires charge.dispute.created -> the handler calls recordReversal, which reads refund_source='admin' at :68 and returns the booking id WITHOUT inserting a disputes row. An even likelier variant: the admin clicks Refund on a charge that is already disputed, `stripe.refunds.create` rejects with charge_disputed (admin-payment-action's own header at :114-119 notes Stripe refuses this), the function 500s — but refund_source='admin' was already persisted at :178, so every subsequent reversal event on that booking is silently swallowed.

title: recordReversal's idempotency key is the CHARGE id, which is identical for every refund of that charge — the second and later refunds are silently swallowed and their amount never reaches the ledger or the control
summary: charge.refunded fires once per refund, always carrying the same `charge.id` and a CUMULATIVE `amount_refunded`. recordReversal dedupes on `ilike '%' + charge.id + '%'` against the disputes reason text, so only the FIRST refund of a charge ever files a row. Every later refund matches the existing row and is dropped. Because ctl_external_reversal_not_ledgered parses the reversal amount out of that reason string (`substring(dd.reason from '([0-9]+\.[0-9]{2}) refunded\)')`), the control's idea of how much Stripe reversed is frozen at the first refund's total and never catches up.
trigger: (1) An operator issues a $10 refund from the Stripe Dashboard. charge.refunded arrives with amount_refunded=10.00 -> disputes row "Stripe refund on charge ch_X (usd 10.00 refunded)". (2) The control fires, the operator records it via the console's Record chargeback op -> refunded_cents=1000, refund_source='chargeback'. (3) The operator issues a SECOND Dashboard refund of $50. charge.refunded arrives with amount_refunded=60.00 and the same ch_X. refund_source is 'chargeback' (not 'admin') so the early-return does not apply, but the `.ilike('reason','%ch_X%')` lookup matches the existing row -> no insert. The stale row still reads 10.00. (4) The control evaluates reversal_cents=1000 against released_cents + refunded_cents = 0 + 1000 and finds 1000 > 1000 false -> no finding.

GMV and admin_dashboard_metrics overstate collected revenue by $50 permanently, and because record_refund is the sole caller of debit_earnings the earner's earnings_total is never reduced for the portion clawed back out of their connected account via reverse_transfer. Scales with every additional partial refund on a charge — only the first is ever ledgerable. reconcile-stripe's refund_mismatch check would flag the drift, but only for payments whose created_at falls inside its 14-day / 200-row window, and only as a finding, not a correction. Secondary defect at the same line: `.maybeSingle()` ERRORS (rather than returning a row) when 2+ disputes rows match, and the error is discarded — so on a booking that already carries a poster-filed dispute plus a webhook reversal row, `existing` comes back null and a redelivered event inserts a DUPLICATE reversal row, which then also skews the control's `order by created_at desc` pick.
evidence:
stripe-webhook/index.ts:85-93 — `const { data: existing } = await supabase.from('disputes').select('id').eq('booking_id', bookingId).ilike('reason', `%${externalId}%`).maybeSingle(); if (!existing) { await supabase.from('disputes').insert({...}) }` — the select's error is never checked.
stripe-webhook/index.ts:317-321 — `const refunded = ((charge.amount_refunded ?? 0) / 100).toFixed(2); const bookingId = await recordReversal(supabase, piId, charge.id, `Stripe refund on charge ${charge.id} (${charge.currency ?? 'usd'} ${refunded} refunded)`);` — externalId is charge.id, constant across every refund of the charge; the per-refund identifier (`event.data.object.refunds.data[0].id`) is never used.
supabase/migrations/20260806040000_control_library.sql:328-331 — `round(substring(dd.reason from '([0-9]+\.[0-9]{2}) refunded\)')::numeric * 100)::bigint as reversal_cents` with `order by dd.booking_id, dd.created_at desc` — the control reads the amount out of the frozen reason text of the single row that was allowed to exist.
fix_sketch: Key idempotency on the individual refund id (the Refund object in the event, or `charge.refunds.data[0].id`) rather than the charge id, and store it in a dedicated indexed column instead of substring-matching free text that also holds user-supplied dispute reasons (Stripe ids contain `_`, which is a single-character LIKE wildcard, so the pattern is looser than intended). At minimum, when a row for this charge already exists and `charge.amount_refunded` exceeds the amount recorded in it, UPDATE the row's reason to the new cumulative total so the control sees the real figure. Also check and act on the select's error instead of discarding it, so a multi-row/`maybeSingle` failure does not fall through to an insert.

The impact claim is where this collapses from medium to low. "The $50 second refund is never written to payments.refunded_cents and never detected" is wrong on the second half: reconcile-stripe's check #4 (index.ts:157-168) reads charge.amount_refunded directly from Stripe, subtracts the partial-capture auto-release, and compares against payments.refunded_cents with TOLERANCE_CENTS = 0. In the traced scenario (full capture, autoReleased 0) it computes realRefundAtStripe 6000 vs ourRefunded 1000 and files a refund_mismatch finding — hourly, via controls_sweep_and_page. This is the Stripe-side reconciler built for exactly the class "the DB is internally consistent and wrong about Stripe", and it is not fooled by the frozen reason text. The residual gap is narrower than claimed: reconcile-stripe's window is payments.created_at >= now()-14d, limit 200, so a second refund issued more than two weeks after the hold was placed can age out unexamined. Report it as "a duplicate-reversal blind spot in ctl_external_reversal_not_ledgered, backstopped by reconcile-stripe except outside its 14-day window", not as an undetected permanent GMV overstatement.
The secondary maybeSingle() claim should be dropped as speculative: reaching 2+ matching rows requires two disputes rows on the same booking both containing the same ch_ id, which the code's own existence check prevents except under a genuine concurrent-redelivery race (no unique index, so possible but unproven). A poster-filed dispute reason from CompletionModal will not contain a Stripe charge id, and the `_`-as-LIKE-wildcard concern needs a reason carrying "ch" + any single char + the remainder of the id verbatim. Also note the suggested fix's `charge.refunds.data[0].id` is not reliable — the refunds list on a Charge is expandable/paginated in current API versions; key on the Refund object from a refund.created event instead.

title: All three tip caps are bypassable by concurrency, and the over-cap money erases its own ledger row
summary: tip_headroom_cents is a lock-free, STABLE read in its own transaction, executed one HTTP round-trip before the card is charged. N concurrent stripe-tip calls all read the same headroom, all pass, and all create+confirm PaymentIntents — so N x headroom actually moves to the earner's connected account. The advisory locks that were supposed to serialise this live in trg_guard_tip_caps, which fires inside claim_and_credit_tip AFTER the money is gone; the losers' `raise exception` rolls back their own tip_ledger insert, so the over-cap money leaves NO row in tip_ledger. It therefore does not count toward the per-booking total, the count-of-3, or the $500/24h velocity cap, and is invisible to every control (all of which query tip_ledger or payments).
trigger: Colluding poster+earner. Post a $10 gig, book it from the alt, poster accepts (authorization only — never captured), both mark done. Booking is now `completed`, which guard_bookings_write allows with NO captured payment (20260730140000, line 96: `old.status='confirmed' and new.status='completed' and new.earner_done and new.poster_done` — the payments-captured EXISTS check applies only to completed->verified). stripe-tip accepts `completed` (index.ts:50). Headroom = greatest(0*2, 20000) = $200 per booking. Now fire 100 concurrent POSTs to stripe-tip with bookingId B and tipCents 20000, 19999, 19998 ... (distinct amounts => distinct idempotency keys => distinct PaymentIntents, and no idempotency-in-progress collisions). All 100 call tip_headroom_cents before any of them has inserted a ledger row; READ COMMITTED plus zero locking means each reads headroom_cents = 20000 and passes `tipCents > remaining`. All 100 PaymentIntents confirm and, being destination charges, transfer in full to the earner's Connect account: ~$20,000 moved. Then all 100 call claim_and_credit_tip; the advisory locks serialise them; exactly ONE inserts and commits; the other 99 hit `tip_cap_booking`/`tip_cap_velocity`, the exception aborts each transaction, and each rolled-back INSERT leaves nothing behind. tip_ledger ends with one $200 row. bookings.tip_amount = 200.00. The 24h velocity counter registers $200. Repeat tomorrow, or on another booking, or with 1000 concurrent calls instead of 100.
money_impact: The earner's connected balance receives N x the cap and pays out daily (no delay_days). The platform's take on all of it is negative (see the no-application_fee finding), and every cent is chargeback-eligible against the PLATFORM balance for 30-90 days because these are destination charges — which is the exact loss 20260804000000's header says the caps exist to bound. The $500/24h ceiling the design believes it enforces becomes $500 x attacker concurrency. With stolen cards this is a cash-out rail: each card only needs one booking driven to `completed`, which costs nothing (no capture required).
evidence:
supabase/functions/stripe-tip/index.ts:86-96 — `const { data: headroom, error: capErr } = await supabase.rpc('tip_headroom_cents', { p_booking: bookingId }); ... const remaining = Number(headroom?.headroom_cents ?? 0); if (Math.round(tipCents) > remaining) {` then :115 `const pi = await stripe.paymentIntents.create({ ... confirm: true, transfer_data: { destination: earnerAcct.account_id } }, { idempotencyKey: `tip_${bookingId}_${Math.round(tipCents)}` });`. Two separate transactions, nothing held between them.
supabase/migrations/20260804000000_tip_caps.sql:168-173 — `create or replace function public.tip_headroom_cents(p_booking uuid) returns jsonb language plpgsql security definer stable` — no pg_advisory_xact_lock anywhere in its body; and as an RPC its transaction ends before the PaymentIntent is created.
supabase/migrations/20260804000000_tip_caps.sql:99-101 — the locks are only in the trigger: `perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('gohustlr.tip.poster:' || v_poster::text, 0)); perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('gohustlr.tip.booking:' || new.booking_id::text, 0));`
supabase/migrations/20260804000000_tip_caps.sql:126-130 / :145-149 — `raise exception 'tip_cap_booking' ...` / `raise exception 'tip_cap_velocity' ...` inside a BEFORE INSERT trigger: the aborted statement leaves no tip_ledger row, so the charge it corresponds to is never counted by :112-115 (`select coalesce(sum(t.amount_cents),0), count(*) ... from public.tip_ledger t where t.booking_id = new.booking_id`) or :137-143 (the 24h poster sum).
supabase/migrations/20260730140000_pin_booking_insert_columns.sql (guard_bookings_write) line 96 vs 97-99 — `completed` needs no captured payment; only `verified` does.
supabase/functions/stripe-tip/index.ts:50 — `if (!['completed','verified'].includes(booking.status))` — `completed` is tippable.
fix_sketch: Reserve headroom in the same transaction that decides. Replace the read-only tip_headroom_cents pre-check with a `reserve_tip_slot(p_booking, p_cents)` RPC that takes the same two advisory locks, re-runs the three caps, and INSERTS a pending tip_ledger row (credited=false, payment_intent_id null / a client-generated reservation key) before the card is touched; stripe-tip then charges and flips the row to the real PI id + credited. A reservation that never gets a PI is expired by a sweeper. Failing that, at minimum have the trigger record the rejected tip (insert into a tip_cap_rejections table via an AFTER-trigger-safe path, or `raise` only after logging) so over-cap money is never invisible, and refund the PaymentIntent from stripe-tip when claim_and_credit_tip returns a tip_cap_* errcode instead of leaving it in the earner's balance.
verifier_note: Three corrections to the impact framing. (1) 'invisible to every control' is wrong: each losing call reaches stripe-tip:146-160 and writes a `fatal: true` row to public.client_errors via logServerError, which builds its OWN service-role client and issues a separate PostgREST insert — a separate transaction that survives the RPC rollback. So 100 concurrent calls leave 99 fatal rows visible at the console's /errors page and counted by admin_dashboard_metrics.errors_fatal_7d (20260804010000:201). It is un-PAGED, not unrecorded. That is still a real defect (no control opens a finding, no email fires), but the money is not untraceable. (2) The per-call bound is the headroom, not $1000: the pre-check refuses `tipCents > remaining`, so on an uncaptured booking each of the N concurrent calls is capped at $200 and N calls move N x $200. The quoted ~$20,000 for 100 concurrent calls is right; the framing '$500 x attacker concurrency' understates the per-booking mechanism and overstates the velocity one. (3) No money is created or stolen from the platform directly — the poster's own card funds every cent. The platform's exposure is Stripe processing on each charge plus 30-90 days of chargeback liability against the platform balance (destination charges), which is realized only on a stolen card or a friendly-fraud dispute. That is why I downgrade critical -> high: it is a bypass of an anti-laundering/chargeback control, not a drain of platform funds on its own. Stripe Radar velocity rules may also decline part of a 100-way concurrent off-session burst on one customer, which no code in this repo can be read to confirm or deny.

title: A refunded or charged-back TIP is never reversed anywhere — and ctl_earnings_total_drift certifies the inflated balance as correct
summary: Every reversal path in the system is keyed on the `payments` table. Tip PaymentIntents are recorded only in tip_ledger, never in payments, so recordReversal() finds nothing and returns null: no `disputes` row, no suppression, no booking attribution. reconcile-stripe iterates `payments` rows only, and admin-payment-action loads a `payments` row before it will refund — so there is no console path to reverse a tip and no reconciler that ever retrieves a tip PI from Stripe. tip_ledger has no refunded/reversed column in any migration. Worse, ctl_earnings_total_drift ADDS every credited tip to `expected` while drawing clawbacks only from payments.refunded_cents, so a fully charged-back tip makes the stored earnings_total match expected exactly — the control actively reports the wrong number as healthy.
trigger: Poster tips $200 on booking B. claim_and_credit_tip credits bookings.tip_amount += 200 and profiles.earnings_today/week/total += 200 (20260722010000:198-210). 40 days later the poster files a chargeback on that tip charge, or an operator refunds it in the Stripe dashboard. Stripe fires charge.dispute.created / charge.refunded. recordReversal looks the PI up in `payments`, finds no row (tips are never inserted into payments), and returns null at :61. The webhook emails 'Booking: not matched — investigate in Stripe' and stops. Nothing decrements tip_amount or earnings_*; tip_ledger still says credited=true, amount_cents=20000, forever. ctl_earnings_total_drift computes expected = captured_credited + tips_credited(20000) - clawed(0, because clawed reads only payments.refunded_cents) and finds abs(stored - expected) = 0, so it never fires.
money_impact: The platform balance is debited the full tip plus Stripe's $15 dispute fee, while the earner keeps the credited amount in their in-app earnings and has already been paid out of the connected account (no transfer reversal exists — the only reverse_transfer in the repo is admin-payment-action/index.ts:186, which is unreachable for a tip because it requires a payments row). profiles.earnings_total, the Tax Center year summary and the year-end tax CSV all overstate the earner's income permanently. Because the drift control counts the reversed tip as expected, the desync is not merely undetected, it is affirmatively cleared.
evidence:
supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts:57-61 — `const { data: payment } = await supabase.from('payments').select('id, booking_id, refund_source').eq('payment_intent_id', paymentIntentId).maybeSingle(); const bookingId = (payment as ...)?.booking_id; if (!bookingId) return null;` — a tip PI is only ever in tip_ledger (20260624211000_tip_ledger.sql:6-13), never in payments.
supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts:281 `case 'charge.dispute.created'` and :309 `case 'charge.refunded'` — both route solely through recordReversal.
supabase/functions/reconcile-stripe/index.ts:71 — `.select("id, booking_id, payment_intent_id, amount_cents, fee_cents, earner_amount_cents, refunded_cents, status, captured_at, created_at")` from payments; tip_ledger is never read.
supabase/functions/admin-payment-action/index.ts:54 — loads a `payments` row before release_hold/refund/record_reversal; a tip has none, so the console cannot reverse it.
supabase/migrations/20260806040000_control_library.sql:268-271 — `tipped as ( select t.earner_id as uid, sum(coalesce(t.amount_cents,0))::bigint as cents from public.tip_ledger t where coalesce(t.credited,false) ... )` and :274-276 `clawed as ( ... from public.payments p ... where coalesce(p.refunded_cents,0) > 0 ...)`, combined at :304 `coalesce(c.cents,0) + coalesce(t.cents,0) - coalesce(r.cents,0) as expected`. No tip can ever appear in `clawed`.
grep of supabase/migrations for tip_ledger shows no column, trigger or function that ever decrements a tip.
fix_sketch: Add `refunded_cents`/`reversed_at` to tip_ledger and have recordReversal fall back to a tip_ledger lookup on payment_intent_id when the payments lookup misses — on hit, call a debit_tip() RPC that reverses bookings.tip_amount and profiles.earnings_* and files the disputes row against the booking. Include reversed tips in ctl_earnings_total_drift's `clawed` CTE, and extend reconcile-stripe to retrieve tip PIs from Stripe and compare amount_refunded against the new column.
verifier_note: One framing correction: the chargeback loss itself (tip amount + Stripe's dispute fee off the platform balance) is inherent to accepting card-funded 100%-pass-through tips and is not caused by this gap — it would be lost even with perfect bookkeeping. The DEFECT is everything downstream: profiles.earnings_total, bookings.tip_amount, the earner's dashboard, and ExpensesScreen's year-end tax CSV permanently overstate income (a 1099 problem, not just a display one); no disputes row is filed so the booking is not flagged; there is no operator path to correct it; and the drift control reports healthy. Also note the finding's own fix sketch is the right shape — a tip_ledger fallback in recordReversal keyed on payment_intent_id would catch it, since the tip PI carries metadata.type='tip' and metadata.booking_id (stripe-tip:124).

title: The only automated detector of a charged-but-not-credited tip is blind to the cause its own registry entry names, because the trigger rolls back the row it queries
summary: ctl_earner_credit_missing's tip branch scans `tip_ledger where credited = false`. The control cannot see it. The controls registry description explicitly claims coverage of this exact stripe-tip path, so the system reports a blind spot as covered. The fallback signal, logServerError, only writes a client_errors row; it does not page.

The loser's PaymentIntent has already confirmed and transferred to the earner's Connect account. claim_and_credit_tip runs; the BEFORE INSERT trigger raises 'tip_cap_booking' (errcode check_violation); PostgreSQL aborts the statement and the whole function's transaction; the tip_ledger row never exists. stripe-tip calls logServerError(..., { fatal: true }) and returns 500. The hourly controls_sweep_and_page runs ctl_earner_credit_missing, which finds nothing to report because its predicate needs a tip_ledger row. No finding is opened, no page fires, and controls_digest reports the money paths healthy.

'remedy', 'service_role: select public.claim_and_credit_tip(...)') from public.tip_ledger t where coalesce(t.credited, false) = false and coalesce(t.created_at, 'epoch'::timestamptz) < now() - interval '15 minutes'`.
supabase/migrations/20260806040000_control_library.sql:621 (registry row) — "stripe-tip charges the card, then calls claim_and_credit_tip (:136). If the function dies, the DB write fails ... Nothing in the system reconciles this on its own" — the claimed coverage.
